decide1.text:
Decide: how the replay shows up

R3, your idea: tap Replay when you're back, the last 20 s play straight away. Not happy? Back to live, recording never stopped.

R3b, my idea: the screen always shows the camera 10 s late, like a gym video-delay mirror. You walk back and watch the lift without touching the phone with chalky hands; tap Keep only for a good one.

Both can ship, as a setting (S1).

facts1.text:
Feasibility, from the Phase 3 spike on the Fairphone

The browser camera gives 30 fps at most; a dim room halves that, so R2 shows the real fps.

A rolling buffer works: WebCodecs' hardware H.264 encoder with a keyframe every second, cut at any keyframe.

Recording, decoding and pose ran together for 35 min: no throttling, about 3.4% battery.

decide2.text:
Your flow, kept: drag the strip under a fixed playhead, Set start, Set end, Analyse. M1 is live: drag it.

Added: step one frame with the arrows; the marked length and how long it takes to analyse show live (about 3 s per second of video on the Fairphone).

Rough marks are enough: the analysis finds the exact lift inside them by itself, so precision costs nothing but a little margin.

facts3.text:
Real data, not filler: A1 to A4 show the engine's real output and pose track for the test clip lateral-raise-cable-1 (one rep, so symmetry can't be scored).

Every threshold in diagnostics.js is still provisional, so every verdict says so until the validation set checks it.

A1 plays: press play or drag the timeline. A4 is one responsive page: wide on a laptop, it stacks at phone width.
